briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax Relief on the Ballot, Rescheduling Nears the Finish Line: Momentum Builds for Operators Coast to Coast
briefs.top: In Michigan, political pressure to kill the 24% wholesale tax is building from both parties even as new stores keep opening in Detroit and along the Ohio border. Nationally, DEA lawyers just told a federal judge marijuana can no longer stay in Schedule I, while Compass Pathways' psilocybin therapy edges toward a historic FDA approval.

local.text: GOP gubernatorial nominee John James made repealing or sharply reducing the 24% wholesale tax a centerpiece of his campaign platform, arguing it 'drives up prices, gives illegal operators a competitive edge, and has already fallen far short of revenue projections' — a signal that tax relief is now a mainstream, bipartisan campaign issue heading into November.

Black-owned High Profile Cannabis Shop celebrated its grand opening on Detroit's eastside, backed by City Council leadership, as social equity licensee Najanava Harvey-Quinn became the operator's first Detroit location under Ann Arbor-based C3 Industries.

C3 Industries opened a new High Profile Cannabis dispensary in Luna Pier, just minutes from Toledo, giving the brand a fresh cross-border retail play with a loyalty program built to capture Ohio traffic and border-town demand.

Michigan's Supreme Court issued rulings this month resetting constitutional guardrails around police searches tied to marijuana, part of a broader August wave of state-level cannabis reforms tracked alongside record sales in Florida and structural shifts in Illinois and Ohio.

A Michigan judge has allowed the cannabis industry's second lawsuit against the 24% wholesale tax to move toward trial, while Rep. James DeSana's one-sentence repeal bill and the tax's own revenue shortfall — roughly $70 million behind projections in the first four months — give operators multiple live paths to relief this year.

national.text: The DEA has submitted its final briefs backing marijuana rescheduling, arguing cannabis has three federally accepted medical uses — treating anorexia, pain, and nausea — capping off formal hearings and pushing the Schedule III shift closer to a judge's recommendation.

Compass Pathways' psilocybin therapy COMP360 is riding a 3-for-3 Phase 3 record and an FDA priority review voucher that could compress its review to just 1-2 months, with analysts eyeing year-end 2026 approval as the first classic psychedelic ever cleared by the FDA.

MDMA-assisted therapy is back in play: Resilient Pharmaceuticals (formerly Lykos) resubmitted its NDA under the brand name Rysanso in August, backed by a third-party audit and new cardiac-safety data, putting the once-rejected treatment back on a roughly six-month FDA review clock.

Curaleaf is pressing its hostile takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis directly to shareholders, touting the deal as a chance to plug into 'a larger, more diversified global cannabis platform' as consolidation among major MSOs accelerates.

Fresh FBI data shows more than 200,000 marijuana arrests nationwide last year, with 92% tied to simple possession — a stark reminder of why advocates say the ongoing federal rescheduling push and state reforms, like Illinois adding sickle cell disease as a qualifying condition, can't move fast enough.
